run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T13:43:24Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by a short burst of HTTP 500s on POST /api/checkout between ~13:43:44Z and ~13:46:13Z. frontend-proxy's own ingress spans show error status while its egress spans to the frontend carry the identical error counts, and the frontend's failing span set is exactly the POST /api/checkout chain ending in grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder. Checkout's only erroring spans are oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and its client span oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge, in identical counts, so every checkout failure observed coincides with a failed charge call. Payment itself records zero error spans, but its charge server spans drop to 0 for the two one-minute windows ending 13:45:00Z and 13:46:00Z while checkout's charge client calls error, and the new payment pod logged its first 'Charge request received' only at 13:46:13.392Z. That pod was created by a Deployment-driven rollout restart at 13:43:41Z (replica-set template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T13:43:41Z, otherwise byte-identical pod template, same 2.1.3-payment image), the old single payment pod was scaled down and deleted at 13:43:44Z, and the payment container defines no readiness, liveness or startup probe, so traffic was cut over before the application was accepting requests. Payment was the only workload replaced during the incident window. Errors returned to baseline (ingress error-ratio 0.0009 at the window ending 13:51:00Z, ingress 5xx-free proxy logs from 13:46:07Z onward) once payment began serving. The alert itself and its underlying expression/metric are not visible in the registered Prometheus, and Jaeger returned no traces for the window, so exact gRPC status texts are unknown.

claims.text: Over the alert window 13:43:24Z-14:04:47Z the registered Prometheus returns span-counter increases for frontend-proxy of ingress STATUS_CODE_ERROR 66.67630020703935 vs ingress STATUS_CODE_UNSET 8372.491727536233, and 'router frontend egress' STATUS_CODE_ERROR 60.521564803312636 vs UNSET 8374.543306004141. These are span counts, not request counts.
frontend-proxy exposes exactly two operations: 'ingress' (span kind server) and 'router frontend egress' (span kind client).

A 5-minute ingress error-ratio series (error spans / all ingress spans) sits at 0.00091352, 0.00061557, 0.00030276, 0 and 0.00029036 for the points from 13:35:00Z to 13:43:00Z, rises to 0.01147118 at 13:45:00Z, 0.01777013 at 13:47:00Z and 0.01783146 at 13:49:00Z, then falls to 0.00086630 at 13:51:00Z.

Before the alert, the frontend-proxy error ratio was already small but non-zero: 5-minute error/total ratios of 0.00035298, 0.00104105, 0.00015053, 0.00030451 and 0.00014512 across 12:43:24Z-13:43:24Z, so the burst is an increase against a non-zero baseline, not a step from zero.

With 2-minute windows, frontend-proxy ingress error spans are 0 at 13:42:00Z, 1.333 at 13:43:00Z and 13:44:00Z, then 52 at 13:45:00Z, 80 at 13:46:00Z and 29.333 at 13:47:00Z, returning to ~1.333 per 2 minutes afterwards; 'router frontend egress' errors are 52, 78.667 and 26.667 on the same three burst points and 0 at every other point.

The only services/operations with non-zero error spans over 13:43:24Z-14:04:47Z are: frontend POST, frontend 'POST /api/checkout', frontend 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' and frontend grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder at 60.521564803312636 each; checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and checkout oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge at 23.222222222222218 each; frontend-proxy ingress 66.67630020703935 and router frontend egress 60.521564803312636; and ad, fraud-detection and recommendation flagd EventStream spans at about 1.03 each.

Checkout's error spans move together: with 2-minute windows oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder errors are 29.199 at 13:45:00Z, 29.333 at 13:46:00Z and 0 at 13:47:00Z, and checkout's client span oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge shows the identical 29.199 / 29.333 / 0 values; every other frontend route (POST /api/cart, GET /api/cart, GET /api/data, GET, tcp.connect) has zero error spans throughout.

Payment's server-side grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge spans (STATUS_CODE_UNSET) are 152 for the 1-minute window ending 13:44:00Z, then 0 for the windows ending 13:45:00Z and 13:46:00Z, then 114.666 for the window ending 13:47:00Z onward, while checkout's charge client spans are in STATUS_CODE_ERROR 44 in the window ending 13:46:00Z.

Payment service spans in the window include zero STATUS_CODE_ERROR for charge, GET, dns.lookup, grpc.flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveFloat, grpc.flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream and tcp.connect; its charge and grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge spans are 381.95687149758453 in STATUS_CODE_UNSET.

Payment pod payment-7b6bfb9fb4-fwlht had no log lines at all before 13:46:13.392Z (its first line is 'Charge request received.' at 13:46:13.392Z); from then on it logs repeated 'Charge request received.' / 'Transaction complete.' pairs through 13:47:59Z and 13:52-13:53Z with no error lines.

The payment pod was replaced by its own controller at 13:43:41Z-13:43:44Z: events show ScalingReplicaSet payment scaled up payment-7b6bfb9fb4 from 0 to 1 and SuccessfulCreate of payment-7b6bfb9fb4-fwlht at 13:43:41Z, Scheduled at 13:43:41Z, Created container at 13:43:43Z, Started container at 13:43:44Z, plus ScalingReplicaSet payment scaled down payment-55766d76b9 from 1 to 0, Killing 'Stopping container payment' and SuccessfulDelete of payment-55766d76b9-cpgm4 at 13:43:44Z.

Payment was the only workload replaced during the incident window: of 21 pods in otel-demo, 20 started between 13:10:41Z and 13:10:44Z, while payment-7b6bfb9fb4-fwlht started 13:43:41Z with restartCount 0; the replica-set listing shows only payment (two replica sets, the new one carrying kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T13:43:41Z) and flagd (restarted at 13:12:30Z, before the alert) with a replacement replica set.

The old and new payment replica-set pod templates are identical apart from the annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T13:43:41Z (same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment, same env, ports, securityContext, requests/limits), which identifies the change as a rollout restart of the same configuration rather than an image change.

The payment Deployment's container 'payment' defines no readinessProbe, no livenessProbe and no startupProbe, has a CPU limit of 20m (memory limit 160Mi), and the Deployment uses RollingUpdate with maxSurge 25% and maxUnavailable 25% at 1 replica; the Deployment currently reports 1 ready and 1 available replica.

frontend-proxy's access log shows POST /api/checkout returning HTTP 500 continuously in the 13:43:40Z-13:45:10Z window (the newest 25 matching lines shown are all 500, spanning 13:44:23.794Z to 13:45:09.929Z; 25 earlier matching lines of that window are not shown), and returning HTTP 200 from 13:46:07.972Z onward (13:46:07Z-13:46:37Z and 13:47:26Z-13:48:29Z slices).

A low-level background of errors predates and outlives the burst: recommendation shows 5-minute error increases of 0 or about 1.07-1.27 alternately from 13:22:24Z through 13:58:24Z, and payment shows 0 error spans at every point of 12:43:24Z-14:04:47Z.

traces_span_metrics_calls_total is the only metric in the registered Prometheus matching the screened span/rpc/http metric-name patterns (no rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count and no http_server_request_duration_seconds_count series are listed for the window), so the alert's own error-rate denominator could not be reproduced from a second metric.

Root cause chain: the payment Deployment was rollout-restarted at 13:43:41Z, its only pod was scaled down and deleted at 13:43:44Z while the replacement pod was counted available immediately because the payment container has no readiness probe; checkout's oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge calls then failed until the new pod first served a charge at 13:46:13.392Z, which produced the checkout PlaceOrder errors, the frontend 500s on POST /api/checkout and consequently the frontend-proxy ingress error spans behind RequestErrorRate. The correlation in time is consistent to the second, but the causal link is an inference from the metric, log and event sequence, not a direct error-string match.

Why the replacement payment container needed about 2 minutes 29 seconds from 'Started container' (13:43:44Z) to its first served charge (13:46:13.392Z) is not directly observed: the container emitted no log lines in that interval and there are no probe events recorded. A slow application start under the 20m CPU limit is a plausible contributor but is unverified.

The alert's reported value 0.01111111111111111 cannot be matched to a metric in this Prometheus; the closest reproducible reading is the 5-minute ingress span-error ratio of 0.01147118 at 13:45:00Z. The alert may therefore be computed from a metric or window not registered here (for example an HTTP server duration counter), and its firing logic cannot be confirmed.

Payment was not itself returning application errors during the window: its error-status spans are zero, it served 381.95687149758453 charge spans with STATUS_CODE_UNSET, and after 13:46:13Z its log contains only successful charge/transaction pairs. The failures therefore occurred before requests reached payment's handler.

frontend-proxy itself was healthy and only propagated upstream errors: its pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-q5c94 is Running with restartCount 0 and start time 13:10:43Z (before the alert), and its ingress error counts (52 / 80 / 29.333) track its frontend-egress error counts (52 / 78.667 / 26.667) in the same 2-minute windows.

Services outside the checkout chain were clean in this window: cart, product-catalog, currency, shipping, email, accounting, quote, image-provider, kafka and load-generator have no non-zero error-span series, and frontend's non-checkout routes (POST /api/cart, GET /api/cart, GET /api/data, GET) show zero error spans, so the burst is confined to the checkout path.

A fault originating in frontend or frontend-proxy was considered and rejected as the cause: frontend's error spans are exactly the four span types of the POST /api/checkout chain with identical counts (60.521564803312636 each), matching the proxy's egress error count, both pods were running with 0 restarts, and checkout's only error-prone dependency call in those traces is the payment charge call.

The chronic flagd EventStream errors on ad, fraud-detection and recommendation were considered and rejected as the cause of this alert: they amount to about one error span per 21 minutes, they exist before and after the burst (recommendation non-zero at 13:24:24Z, 13:36:24Z and again at 13:52:24Z-13:58:24Z), and they are on flagd streaming spans, not on the frontend→checkout→payment request path that produced the proxy 5xx.

Add a readinessProbe (and optionally a startupProbe on the payment HTTP/gRPC 8080 port) to the payment container so a rolling restart cannot remove the last serving replica before the replacement accepts traffic, and avoid restarting the single payment replica without such gating.

Establish why the payment container needed roughly 2.5 minutes before serving charges after start (restart timing under the 20m CPU limit, or a blocking startup dependency), and confirm the alert rule's expression/metric so a 5xx burst of this size and duration is understood rather than inferred.

gaps: Jaeger returned no traces for frontend-proxy, checkout or frontend in 13:40Z-14:04Z (backend_traces_returned 0 for each), although all three services are listed by Jaeger, so the exact gRPC status codes and error texts of the failing PlaceOrder/Charge calls are unknown.

The RequestErrorRate alerting rule is not present in the registered Prometheus (list_prometheus_rules for rule_name RequestErrorRate returned no data), and no rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count or http_server_request_duration_seconds_count series exist here, so the alert's expression, threshold, window and the 0.01111111111111111 value are unverified.

The alert's start time 13:43:24Z precedes the payment replica-set creation at 13:43:41Z and the first observed proxy 500 at 13:44:23Z; the timing relationship between Alertmanager evaluation and cluster/Prometheus clocks is unresolved.

The change_history integration is not integrated in this Run, so who or what issued the kubectl rollout restart on the payment Deployment is unknown beyond the kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T13:43:41Z annotation.

The new payment container produced no startup log lines before 13:46:13.392Z and there are no probe events, so the reason it did not accept charge requests for about 2.5 minutes is not directly evidenced.

The frontend container yielded zero log lines in 13:43:30Z-13:47:30Z (stream read, 0 lines), so no frontend-side error text is available; checkout's log had 3733 lines in 13:35Z-14:00Z with none matching error patterns, so checkout's own error text is also unknown.
The old payment pod payment-55766d76b9-cpgm4 was deleted, so its logs, shutdown behaviour and whether it drained in-flight charges cannot be checked.

kube-state-metrics series (kube_pod_owner, kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready, kube_pod_container_info) and app_payment_transactions_total returned no metric names for this window, so pod-ready history, image digests and payment transaction counters could not be verified.

frontend-proxy also carries a steady background of about 1.33 ingress error spans per 2 minutes that is not matched by egress errors (for example 13:48Z-14:04Z); its cause was not investigated and is unrelated to this burst.
next_steps: Add a readinessProbe/startupProbe on port 8080 to the otel-demo payment container (or otherwise gate rollout on application readiness) so a single-replica restart cannot send charge traffic to a pod that is not yet listening.
Measure payment container start-to-listening time and review the 20m CPU / 160Mi memory limits as a possible cause of the roughly 2.5-minute delay before it served charges.
Identify who ran the rollout restart on Deployment otel-demo/payment at 2026-11-16T13:43:41Z (change-history/audit source is not integrated here).
Retrieve the RequestErrorRate rule definition and its underlying metric/window from the alerting Prometheus or Alertmanager configuration to confirm the 0.01111111111111111 reading and threshold.
Re-run trace lookups for 13:43Z-13:47Z once Jaeger retains data for that interval, to capture the exact gRPC status of the failed checkout→payment charge calls.
